title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 60 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 427–430 (Night 60, continuing directly from nights-59), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 60 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sultan Sharkān has the merchant’s charter written, then has a curtain hung and the ladies of the court come to meet Nuzhat al-Zamān; at the king’s bidding she begins the first chapter of her learning, on kingship and the duties of rulers. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُوفِيَةُ لِلسِّتِّينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-mūfiyatu li-al-sittīna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the completing-one for the sixty,
sentences.i: And when it was the sixtieth night,
sentences.n: الْمُوفِيَة, "the completing one", is the night that makes up the full count; li-al-sittīn, "for the sixty", gives the number. Together they mean "the night that completes sixty", the sixtieth.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ شَرْكَانَ أَمَرَ الْمُتَاجِرَ بِكِتَابَةِ مَنْشُورٍ بَعْدَ مَا سَلَّمَ لَهُ الْمَالَ وَكَتَبَ لَهُ التَّوْقِيعَ مُخَلِّدًا أَنَّهُ لَا يَدْفَعُ عَلَى تِجَارَتِهِ عُشْرًا وَلَا يَتَعَرَّضُ لَهُ أَحَدٌ بِسُوءٍ فِي مَمْلَكَتِهِ وَأَمَرَ لَهُ بِخِلْعَةٍ سَنِيَّةٍ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-malika Sharkāna amara al-mutājira bi-kitābati manshūrin baʿda mā sallama lahu al-māla wa-kataba lahu al-tawqīʿa mukhalladan annahu lā yadfaʿu ʿalā tijāratihi ʿushran wa-lā yataʿarraḍu lahu aḥadun bi-sūʾin fī mamlakatihi wa-amara lahu bi-khilʿatin saniyyatin
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate-one, that the king Sharkān commanded the trader to the writing of a decree, after he had handed-over to him the money and written for him the rescript, making-it-lasting that he would not pay upon his trade a tenth, and no one would expose himself to him with evil in his kingdom; and he commanded for him a robe-of-honour, resplendent.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that King Sharkān ordered the merchant to write out a decree, once he had handed over the money and written him the rescript. It was to stand forever that he would pay no tenth on his trade and that no one in his kingdom would do him any harm. The king also ordered a splendid robe of honour for him.
sentences.n: السَّعِيدَأَنَّ is printed as one word, السَّعِيدَ أَنَّ "the fortunate, that"; it is kept as printed. أَمَرَ بِـ is "command (someone) to do", with بِـ introducing the thing commanded: here "the writing of a decree" and later "a robe of honour". الْمُتَاجِر is the trader, the same man the story calls التَّاجِر. مُخَلِّدًا is read as "making lasting": the decree is set down as permanent, and the clause with أَنَّ says what it fixes. The "tenth" (عُشْر) is the tithe levied on merchants' goods. يَتَعَرَّضُ لَهُ بِسُوءٍ is "expose himself to him with evil", that is, molest or injure him.

sentences.t: وَانْصَرَفَ جَمِيعُ مَنْ عِنْدَهُ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ عِنْدَهُ غَيْرُ الْقُضَاةِ وَالتَّاجِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-inṣarafa jamīʿu man ʿindahu wa-lam yabqa ʿindahu ghayru al-quḍāti wa-al-tājiri
sentences.l: and all of whoever was with him went-away, and there did not remain with him other-than the judges and the merchant.
sentences.i: Everyone who had been with him left, and no one remained with him but the judges and the merchant.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِلْقُضَاةِ أُرِيدُأَنْ تَسْمَعُوا مِنْ أَلْفَاظِ هٰذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ مَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى عِلْمِهَا وَأَدَبِهَا مِنْ كُلِّ مَا ادَّعَاهُ التَّاجِرُ لِنُحَقِّقَ صِدْقَ كَلَامِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-al-quḍāti urīdu an tasmaʿū min alfāẓi hādhihi al-jāriyati mā yadullu ʿalā ʿilmihā wa-adabihā min kulli mā iddaʿāhu al-tājiru li-nuḥaqqiqa ṣidqa kalāmihi
sentences.l: And he said to the judges: I want that you hear, from the words of this girl, what indicates her knowledge and her culture, out of all that the merchant claimed, so that we verify the truth of his speech.
sentences.i: He said to the judges, "I want you to hear from this girl's own words something that shows her learning and her breeding, out of all that the merchant has claimed, so that we may confirm the truth of what he says."
sentences.n: اريدان is printed as one word, أُرِيدُ أَنْ "I want that"; it is kept as printed. After أَنْ the verb is subjunctive (تَسْمَعُوا). الْجَارِيَة is a young woman, here the slave-girl Nuzhat al-Zamān. أَدَب is good breeding and polite learning, what a cultivated person knows and how they speak.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَابَأْسَ بِذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lā baʾsa bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And they said: No harm in that.
sentences.i: They said, "There is no harm in that."
sentences.n: لَابَأْسَ is printed as one word, لَا بَأْسَ "no harm"; here it means "no objection".

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ بِإِرْخَاءِ سِتَارَةٍ بَيْنَهُ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْجَارِيَةِ وَمَنْ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-amara bi-irkhāʾi sitāratin baynahu huwa wa-man maʿahu wa-bayna al-jāriyati wa-man maʿahā
sentences.l: And he commanded the letting-down of a curtain between him, he, and whoever was with him, and between the girl and whoever was with her,
sentences.i: Then he ordered a curtain to be let down between himself and those with him, and the girl and those with her.
sentences.n: بَيْنَهُ هُوَ, "between him, he", repeats the pronoun for emphasis so that it can be joined to وَمَنْ مَعَهُ "and whoever was with him". أَمَرَ بِـ again: the thing commanded is "the letting down of a curtain".

sentences.t: وَصَارَ جَمِيعُ النِّسَاءِ اللَّاتِي مَعَ الْجَارِيَةِ خَلْفَ السِّتَارَةِ يُهَنِّينَهَا وَيُقَبِّلْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَرِجْلَيْهَا لَمَّا عَلِمُوا أَنَّهَا صَارَتْ زَوْجَةَ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra jamīʿu al-nisāʾi allātī maʿa al-jāriyati khalfa al-sitārati yuhanniyinahā wa-yuqabbilna yadayhā wa-rijlayhā lammā ʿalimū annahā ṣārat zawjata al-maliki
sentences.l: and all the women who were with the girl, behind the curtain, became congratulating-her and kissing her two hands and her two feet, when they knew that she had become the wife of the king;
sentences.i: and all the women who were with the girl, behind the curtain, began to congratulate her and kiss her hands and feet, since they knew she had become the king's wife;
sentences.n: صَارَ plus an imperfect verb means "begin to, keep on". يُهَنِّينَهَا is printed يهنّينها; it is read as the defective II verb "congratulate" (يُهَنِّينَ, with the ن of the feminine plural). The usual spelling would carry a hamza, يُهَنِّئْنَهَا; the rasm is the same either way. عَلِمُوا is masculine plural although the subject is women (Classical عَلِمْنَ): a Middle Arabic feature to move past. The shadda on اللَّاتِي and on the first ن of يُهَنِّينَهَا is the print's own.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دُرْنَ حَوْلَهَا وَقَلَعْنَ ثِيَابَهَا وَخَفَّفْنَهَا مِنْ ثِقَلِ الثِّيَابِ وَصِرْنَ يَنْظُرْنَ إِلَى حُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma durna ḥawlahā wa-qalaʿna thiyābahā wa-khaffafnahā min thiqli al-thiyābi wa-ṣirna yanẓurna ilā ḥusnihā wa-jamālihā
sentences.l: Then they went-round about her and pulled-off her clothes and lightened her of the weight of the clothes, and began looking at her beauty and her loveliness.
sentences.i: Then they gathered around her, took off her clothes and relieved her of their weight, and stood gazing at her beauty and loveliness.
sentences.n: دُرْنَ and صِرْنَ are the feminine plural past forms of the hollow verbs دَارَ and صَارَ. Note that these verbs, unlike عَلِمُوا just before, agree in the feminine.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَتْ نِسَاءُ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ شَرْكَانَ اشْتَرَى جَارِيَةً مَا مِثْلُهَا فِى الْجَمَالِ وَالْعِلْمِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْحِسَابِ وَأَنَّهَا حَوَتْ جَمِيعَ الْعُلُومِ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿat nisāʾu al-umarāʾi wa-al-wuzarāʾi anna al-malika Sharkāna ishtarā jāriyatan mā mithluhā fī al-jamāli wa-al-ʿilmi wa-al-ḥikmati wa-al-ḥisābi wa-annahā ḥawat jamīʿa al-ʿulūmi
sentences.l: And the women-of the emirs and the viziers heard that the king Sharkān had bought a girl, not the like-of-her in the beauty and the knowledge and the wisdom and the reckoning, and that she had contained all the sciences,
sentences.i: The wives of the emirs and viziers heard that King Sharkān had bought a slave-girl without her equal in beauty, learning, wisdom and arithmetic, and that she had mastered every branch of knowledge,
sentences.n: مَا مِثْلُهَا is a nominal clause describing the girl: "there is no one like her". الْحِسَاب is reckoning, arithmetic. The sentence begins mid-narration, continuing the account of the preceding lines.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ وَزَنَ ثَمَنَهَا ثَلٰثُمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَأَعْتَقَهَا وَكَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad wazana thamanahā thalāthumiʾati dīnārin wa-ʿishrīna alfa dīnārin wa-aʿtaqahā wa-kataba kitābahu ʿalayhā
sentences.l: and indeed he had weighed-out her price, three-hundred of dinars and twenty thousand of dinars, and had freed her, and had written his writing upon her.
sentences.i: and that he had paid out her price, three hundred and twenty thousand dinars, set her free, and drawn up his deed over her.
sentences.n: ثلثمائة is printed in the defective way, without the alif of ثَلَاث; the dagger alif on the lām supplies it. "Three hundred and twenty thousand" is the sum the text states: ثَلٰثُمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ, literally "three hundred of dinars and twenty thousand of dinars", the wording of the print. وَزَنَ, "weighed", is the usual verb for paying out coin, which was weighed. كَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ عَلَيْهَا, "wrote his writing upon her", is the written deed (of freedom and marriage) drawn up for her.

sentences.t: وَأَحْضَرَ الْقُضَاةَ الْأَرْبَعَةَ لِأَجْلِ امْتِحَانِهَا حَتَّى تُجَاوِبَهُمْ عَلَى مَا يَسْأَلُونَهَا وَيُنَاظِرُونَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-aḥḍara al-quḍāta al-arbaʿata li-ajli imtiḥānihā ḥattā tujāwibahum ʿalā mā yasʾalūnahā wa-yunāẓirūnahā
sentences.l: and had-present the judges, the four, for the sake-of testing-her, so-that she answer them upon what they ask her and dispute with her.
sentences.i: and he summoned the four judges to put her to the test, so that she might answer them on whatever they asked and argued with her.
sentences.n: The four judges are the heads of the four Sunni schools of law. يَسْأَلُونَهَا is "they ask her", the question itself being the unspoken object. يُنَاظِرُونَهَا (verb III) is to engage in formal disputation.

sentences.t: فَطَلَبَ النِّسَاءُ الْإِذْنَ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِهِنَّ وَمَضَيْنَ إِلَي الْقَصْرِ الَّذِي فِيهِ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaba al-nisāʾu al-idhna min azwājihinna wa-maḍayna ilā al-qaṣri alladhī fīhi Nuzhatu al-Zamāni
sentences.l: And the women sought the permission from their husbands and went off to the palace which in-it Nuzhat al-Zamān was.
sentences.i: So the women asked their husbands' leave and went to the palace where Nuzhat al-Zamān was.
sentences.n: إِلَي is printed with a dotted yā for the usual إِلَى (alif maqṣūra); the letter is kept as printed. The verb طَلَبَ is singular because it comes before its plural subject النِّسَاءُ, as regular Arabic wants; the following verb, وَمَضَيْنَ, takes the feminine plural ending -na.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْنَ عَلَيْهَا وَجَدْنَ الْخَدَمَ وُقُوفًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalna ʿalayhā wajadna al-khadama wuqūfan bayna yadayhā
sentences.l: And when they entered upon her, they found the servants standing between her two hands.
sentences.i: When they went in to her, they found the servants standing in attendance before her.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا, "between her two hands", is the idiom for "in front of her", usually of those who stand in service.

sentences.t: فَحِينَ رَأَتْ نِسَاءَ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ وَأَرْبَابَ الدَّوْلَةِ دَاخِلَةً عَلَيْهَا قَامَتْ لَهُنَّ عَلَى أَقْدَامِهَا وَقَابَلَتْهُنَّ وَوَقَفَتِ الْجَوَارِي خَلْفَهَا وَتَلَقَّتِ النِّسَاءَ بِالتَّرْحِيبِ وَصَارَتْ تَتَبَسَّمُ فِي وُجُوهِهِنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥīna raʾat nisāʾa al-umarāʾi wa-al-wuzarāʾi wa-arbāba al-dawlati dākhilatan ʿalayhā qāmat lahunna ʿalā aqdāmihā wa-qābalathunna wa-waqafati al-jawārī khalfahā wa-talaqqati al-nisāʾa bi-al-tarḥībi wa-ṣārat tatabassamu fī wujūhihinna
sentences.l: And when she saw the women-of the emirs and the viziers and the lords-of the state entering upon her, she stood for them upon her feet and met them, and the girls stood behind her, and she received the women with the welcome, and began smiling in their faces,
sentences.i: When she saw the wives of the emirs, the viziers and the lords of the state coming in to her, she rose to her feet for them and went to meet them, while her maidservants stood behind her. She received the women with a warm welcome and kept smiling in their faces,
sentences.n: دَاخِلَةً is a singular feminine participle agreeing with the collective نِسَاء, "women". أَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ, "lords of the state", means the great men of the realm. صَارَتْ تَتَبَسَّمُ, "became smiling", is "began to smile" or "kept smiling".

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ بِقُلُوبِهِنَّ ثُمَّ أَوْعَدَتْهُنَّ بِكُلِّ خَيْرٍ وَأَنْزَلَتْهُنَّ فِي مَرَاتِبِهِنَّ كَأَنَّهَا تَرَبَّتْ مَعَهُنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat bi-qulūbihinna thumma awʿadathunna bi-kulli khayrin wa-anzalathunna fī marātibihinna ka-annahā tarabbat maʿahunna
sentences.l: and she took them by their hearts, then promised them with every good, and had-them-alight in their ranks, as-though she had been brought-up with them,
sentences.i: and she won their hearts. Then she promised them every kindness and seated them each according to rank, as though she had grown up with them,
sentences.n: أَخَذَ بِقَلْبِهِ, "take by the heart", is "captivate". أَوْعَدَ is classically "threaten" (the form that means "promise" is وَعَدَ); here, with بِكُلِّ خَيْرٍ, it plainly means promise, a later usage. أَنْزَلَهُنَّ فِي مَرَاتِبِهِنَّ, "made them alight in their ranks", is to give each her due place.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْنَ مِنْ عَقْلِهَا وَأَدَبِهَا مَعَ حُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabna min ʿaqlihā wa-adabihā maʿa ḥusnihā wa-jamālihā
sentences.l: and they marvelled at her intellect and her good-breeding along-with her comeliness and her beauty.
sentences.i: and they marvelled at her good sense and breeding, as well as her loveliness and beauty.
sentences.n: The sajʿ-like pairs عَقْلِهَا وَأَدَبِهَا and حُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا end in the same -ihā. أَدَب is good breeding, courtesy and polish.

sentences.t: وَقُلْنَ بَعْضُهُنَّ لِبَعْضٍ مَا هَذِهِ جَارِيَةٌ بَلْ مَلِكَةٌ بِنْتُ مَلِكٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qulna baʿḍuhunna li-baʿḍin mā hādhihi jāriyatun bal malikatun bintu malikin
sentences.l: and they said, some-of-them to some: This is not a girl, rather a queen, a daughter-of a king.
sentences.i: and they said to one another, "This is no slave-girl, but a queen, a king's daughter."
sentences.n: بَعْضُهُنَّ لِبَعْضٍ is the standard way to say "to one another". مَا هَذِهِ جَارِيَةٌ has مَا with a nominative predicate: "this is not a slave-girl". This negative mā followed by a nominative predicate is a construction that also turns up in Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسْنَ يُعَظِّمْنَ قَدْرَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-jalasna yuʿaẓẓimna qadrahā
sentences.l: And they sat magnifying her worth
sentences.i: They sat down, paying honour to her station,

sentences.t: وَقُلْنَ لَهَا يَا سَيِّدَتَنَا أَضَاءَتْ بِكِ بَلْدَتُنَا وَشَرُفَتْ بِلَادُنَا وَأَمَاكِنُنَا وَأَوْطَانُنَا وَمَمْلَكَتُنَا فَالْمَمْلَكَةُ مَمْلَكَتُكِ وَالْقَصْرُ قَصْرُكِ وَكُلُّنَا جَوَارِيكِ فَبِاللَّهِ لَا تُخَلِّيَنَا مِنْ إِحْسَانِكِ وَالنَّظَرِ إِلَى حُسْنِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qulna lahā yā sayyidatanā aḍāʾat bi-ki baldatunā wa-sharufat bilādunā wa-amākinunā wa-awṭānunā wa-mamlakatunā fa-al-mamlakatu mamlakatuki wa-al-qaṣru qaṣruki wa-kullunā jawāriki fa-bi-Allāhi lā tukhalliyanā min iḥsānika wa-al-naẓari ilā ḥusniki
sentences.l: and they said to her: O our lady, our town has shone through you, and our lands have become-honoured, and our places and our homelands and our kingdom; so the kingdom is your kingdom and the palace is your palace and all-of-us are your girls; so by God, do not leave-us-void of your kindness and the looking at your beauty!
sentences.i: and they said to her, "O our lady, our town is lit up because of you, and our country is honoured, and all our places, our homelands and our kingdom. The kingdom is your kingdom, the palace is your palace, and every one of us is your handmaid. By God, do not deny us your kindness and the sight of your beauty!"
sentences.n: بِكِ is the preposition with the feminine ending -ki, "through you". The verb أَضَاءَتْ is written as the intransitive "shone". The long list of subjects after the verb شَرُفَتْ is read as one set, the feminine singular verb agreeing with the nearest noun. تُخَلِّيَنَا keeps the yā of the verb stem in the print; strict grammar would write لَا تُخَلِّنَا (jussive). فَبِاللَّهِ is an oath: بِـ introduces the one sworn by, "by God". النَّظَرِ إِلَى حُسْنِكِ, "the looking at your beauty", is coordinated with إِحْسَانِكِ under مِنْ.

sentences.t: فَشَكَرَتْهُنَّ عَلَى ذَٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-shakarathunna ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And she thanked them for that.
sentences.i: and she thanked them for it.

sentences.t: هَذَا كُلُّهُ وَالسِّتَارَةُ مُرْخَاةٌ بَيْنَهَا وَمَنْ عِنْدَهَا مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَبَيْنَ الْمَلِكِ شَرْكَانَ وَالْقُضَاةِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ وَالتَّاجِرِ وَهُمْ جَالِسُونَ بِجَانِبِ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: hādhā kulluhu wa-al-sitāratu murkhātun baynahā wa-man ʿindahā mina al-nisāʾi wa-bayna al-maliki Sharkāna wa-al-quḍāti al-arbaʿati wa-al-tājiri wa-hum jālisūna bi-jānibi al-maliki
sentences.l: This, all of it, and the curtain lowered between her and those who were with her of the women, and between the king Sharkān and the judges, the four, and the merchant, and they sitting by the side-of the king.
sentences.i: All this took place while the curtain hung lowered between her and the women with her on one side, and King Sharkān, the four judges and the merchant on the other, who were seated beside the king.
sentences.n: هَذَا كُلُّهُ is a loose opening, "all this (happened)", followed by a circumstantial clause with وَ. بَيْنَهَا وَمَنْ عِنْدَهَا: one "between" serves both "her" and "those with her" (the women), and a second وَبَيْنَ opens the other side, the king and his company. The slice ends here, in mid-sentence, at a line break.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَادَاهَا الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ وَقَالَ لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nādāhā al-maliku Sharkānu wa-qāla lahā
sentences.l: So at that, called-her the king Sharkān and he-said to-her
sentences.i: Thereupon King Sharkān called to her and said to her:

sentences.t: أَيَّتُهَا الْمَمْلَكَةُ الْعَزِيزَةُ فِي زَمَانِهَا إِنَّ هَذَا التَّاجِرَ قَدْ وَصَفَكِ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالْأَدَبِ وَادَّعَى أَنَّكِ تَعْرِفِينَ فِي جَمِيعِ الْعُلُومِ حَتَّى عِلْمِ النُّجُومِ
sentences.tr: ayyatuhā al-mamlakatu al-ʿazīzatu fī zamānihā inna hādhā al-tājira qad waṣafaki bi-al-ʿilmi wa-al-adabi wa-iddaʿā annaki taʿrifīna fī jamīʿi al-ʿulūmi ḥattā ʿilmi al-nujūmi
sentences.l: O-you queen, the dear-one in her time: indeed this merchant, he-has described-you with the knowledge and the letters, and he-claimed that-you know in all of-the-sciences, even the science of-the-stars
sentences.i: O queen, dear and precious in your age, this merchant has described you as a woman of learning and refinement, and he claims that you know all the sciences, even the science of the stars.
sentences.n: ايتها is printed without hamza; read ayyatuhā (the feminine of ayyuhā), 'O you'. وادّعى is the one word the edition itself marks, with a shadda on the dāl.

sentences.t: فَاسْمَعِينَا شَيْأً مِمَّا ذَكَرْتِهِ لِذَلِكَ التَّاجِرِ وَاذْكُرِي لَنَا مِنْ هَذَا الشَّيْءِ بَابًا يَسِيرًا
sentences.tr: fa-asmiʿīnā shayʾan mimmā dhakartihi li-dhālika al-tājiri wa-udhkurī lanā min hādhā al-shayʾi bāban yasīran
sentences.l: So-make-us-hear something of-what you-mentioned to that merchant, and mention to-us from this thing a chapter, easy
sentences.i: So let us hear something of what you told that merchant, and give us a short chapter from it.
sentences.n: The edition prints شيأ (with a precomposed hamza on the final letter) for شيئًا; we read shayʾan.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ قَالَتْ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahu qālat samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And when she-heard his speech she-said: hearing and obedience
sentences.i: When she heard his words she said, "With hearing and obedience,

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْبَابُ الْأَوَّلُ فِى السِّيَاسَاتِ وَالْآدَابِ الْمَلَكِيَّةِ وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لِوُلَاةِ الْأُمُورِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ وَمَا يَلْزَمُ أَهَمَّ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْأَخْلَاقِ الْمَرْضِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku al-bābu al-awwalu fī al-siyāsāti wa-al-ādābi al-malakiyyati wa-mā yanbaghī li-wulāti al-umūri al-sharʿiyyati wa-mā yalzamu ahamma min qibali al-akhlāqi al-marḍiyyati
sentences.l: O king, the chapter the first is in the policies and the refinements, the royal-ones, and what is-fitting for the governors of-the-affairs, the lawful-ones, and what is-necessary, most-important, from the side of-the-characters, the approved-ones
sentences.i: O king, the first chapter concerns royal policy and courtly conduct, what befits those who govern lawful affairs, and what is most needful on the side of approved character.
sentences.n: The words وما يلزم اهم are obscure. Taken as printed they read 'and what is necessary, the most important (ahamm)'; the closing chapter-title may be corrupt, perhaps for يلزمهم 'what is incumbent on them' (the governors). We vocalise what is printed.

sentences.t: إِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ مَحَاسِنَ الْخُلُقِ مَجْمُوعَةٌ فِى الدِّينِ وَالدُّنْيَا
sentences.tr: iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna maḥāsina al-khuluqi majmūʿatun fī al-dīni wa-al-dunyā
sentences.l: Know, O king, that the fair-points of-the-character are gathered in the religion and the world
sentences.i: Know, O king, that the virtues of character are gathered together in religion and in worldly life.
sentences.n: Written اعلم (alif without hamza), read iʿlam, the imperative 'know'. In الخلق we read al-khuluq, 'character'.

sentences.t: فَلَا يَتَوَصَّلُ أَحَدٌ إِلَى الدِّينِ إِلَّا بِالدُّنْيَا لِأَنَّهَا نِعْمَ الطَّرِيقُ إِلَى الْآخِرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lā yatawaṣṣalu aḥadun ilā al-dīni illā bi-al-dunyā li-annahā niʿma al-ṭarīqu ilā al-ākhirati
sentences.l: So not reaches anyone to the religion except by the world, because-it is excellent the road to the hereafter
sentences.i: No one can reach religion except by way of this world, for it is an excellent road to the hereafter.

sentences.t: وَلَيْسَ يَنْتَظِمُ أَمْرُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا بِأَعْمَالِ أَهْلِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-laysa yantaẓimu amru al-dunyā illā bi-aʿmāli ahlihā
sentences.l: And not is ordered the affair of-the-world except by the works of its people
sentences.i: And the affairs of this world are not set in order except by the labours of its people.

sentences.t: وَأَعْمَالُ النَّاسِ تَنْقَسِمُ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْسَامٍ الْإِمَارَةُ وَالتِّجَارَةُ وَالزِّرَاعَةُ وَالصِّنَاعَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿmālu al-nāsi tanqasimu ʿalā arbaʿati aqsāmin al-imāratu wa-al-tijāratu wa-al-zirāʿatu wa-al-ṣināʿatu
sentences.l: And the works of-the-people divide upon four divisions: the governorship and the trade and the tillage and the craft
sentences.i: And the occupations of people divide into four kinds: government, trade, farming and craft.

sentences.t: فَالْإِمَارَةُ يَنْبَغِي لَهَا السِّيَاسَةُ التَّامَّةُ وَالْفِرَاسَةُ الصَّادِقَةُ لِأَنَّ الْإِمَارَةَ مَدَارُ عِمَارَةِ الدُّنْيَا الَّتِي هِيَ طَرِيقٌ إِلَى الْآخِرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-al-imāratu yanbaghī lahā al-siyāsatu al-tāmmatu wa-al-firāsatu al-ṣādiqatu li-anna al-imārata madāru ʿimārati al-dunyā allatī hiya ṭarīqun ilā al-ākhirati
sentences.l: So the governorship, is-fitting for-it the policy, the complete, and the discernment, the true, because the governorship is the pivot of the peopling of-the-world which is a road to the hereafter
sentences.i: Government calls for complete statecraft and sound discernment, because government is the pivot on which the building-up of this world turns, and this world is a road to the hereafter.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى جَعَلَ الدُّنْيَا الْمَعْبَادَ كَزَادِ الْمُسَافِرِ أَىْ تَحْصِيلِ الْمُرَادِ
sentences.tr: li-anna Allāha taʿālā jaʿala al-dunyā al-maʿbāda ka-zādi al-musāfiri ay taḥṣīli al-murādi
sentences.l: Because God, exalted, made the world, the maʿbād, like the provision of-the-traveller, that-is the attainment of-the-aim
sentences.i: For God, exalted is He, made this world, the place of passage, like a traveller's provisions, that is, a means of attaining the goal.
sentences.n: المعباد is odd. It may be a misprint for المعاد 'the (place of) return, the hereafter', or a form from العبادة 'worship' (cf. معبد 'place of worship'); we vocalise it as printed (al-maʿbād) and render it loosely. Here كَـ is the 'like' prefix: كزاد 'like the provision'.

sentences.t: فَيَنْبَغِي لِكُلِّ إِنْسَانٍ أَنْ يَتَنَاوَلَ مِنْهَا بِقَدْرِ مَا يُوصِلُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَلَا يَتَّبِعَ فِي ذَلِكَ نَفْسَهُ وَهَوَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-yanbaghī li-kulli insānin an yatanāwala minhā bi-qadri mā yūṣiluhu ilā Allāhi wa-lā yattabiʿa fī dhālika nafsahu wa-hawāhu
sentences.l: So it-is-fitting for every person that he-take from-it by the measure of-what brings-him to God, and not follow in that his self and his desire
sentences.i: So it is fitting for every person to take from it only as much as brings him to God, and not to follow, in doing so, his own self and desire.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ تَنَاوَلَهَا النَّاسُ بِالْعَدْلِ لَانْقَطَعَتِ الْخُصُومَاتُ
sentences.tr: wa-law tanāwalahā al-nāsu bi-al-ʿadli la-inqaṭaʿati al-khuṣūmātu
sentences.l: And if took-it the people with the justice, would-be-cut-off the disputes
sentences.i: If people took from it with justice, disputes would cease.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنَّهُمْ يَتَنَاوَلُونَهَا بِالْجَوْرِ وَمُتَابَعَةِ الْهَوَى فَتَسَبَّبَتْ عَنْ انْهِمَاكِهِمْ عَلَيْهَا الْخُصُومَاتُ
sentences.tr: wa-lakinnahum yatanāwalūnahā bi-al-jawri wa-mutābaʿati al-hawā fa-tasabbabat ʿan inhimākihim ʿalayhā al-khuṣūmātu
sentences.l: But-they take-it with the injustice and the following of-the-desire, so arose from their immersion upon-it the disputes
sentences.i: But they take it with injustice and by following their desires, and so disputes arose from their being absorbed in it.

sentences.t: فَاحْتَاجُوا إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ يُنْصِفَ بَيْنَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-iḥtājū ilā al-sulṭāni li-ajli an yunṣifa baynahum
sentences.l: So they-needed to the sultan for the sake that he-deal-justly between them
sentences.i: So they needed the sultan, so that he might deal justly between them.

sentences.t: وَيَضْبِطُ أُمُورَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-yaḍbiṭu umūrahum
sentences.l: and he regulates their affairs,
sentences.i: and manages their affairs.
sentences.n: Continues a sentence begun on the previous page: the king (the subject, the good ruler) 'manages their affairs'.

sentences.t: وَلَوْلَارَدْعُ الْمَلِكِ النَّاسَ عَنْ بَعْضِهِمْ أَغْلَبَ قَوِيُّهُمْ عَلَى ضَعِيفِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-lawlāradʿu al-maliki al-nāsa ʿan baʿḍihim aghlaba qawiyyuhum ʿalā ḍaʿīfihim
sentences.l: and had-it-not-been-for the restraining of the king the people from some-of-them, would-have-overcome their strong-one over their weak-one,
sentences.i: And were it not for the king restraining people from one another, the strong among them would overpower the weak.
sentences.n: The print runs lawlā and radʿ together as one word (ولولاردع). The apodosis normally takes lām (لَغَلَبَ, 'would have overcome'); the print has اغلب, which I read as aghlaba. It may be a misprint for that, or for يَغْلِبُ 'overcomes'; the sense is the same.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَالَ أَزْدَ شِيرُ أَنَّ الدِّينَ وَالْمُلْكَ تَوْأَمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qāla Azda Shīru anna al-dīna wa-al-mulka tawʾamāni
sentences.l: and indeed said Azd Shīr that the religion and the kingship are twins:
sentences.i: Ardashīr said that religion and kingship are twins:
sentences.n: The Persian king's name Ardashīr is printed as two words, ازد شير, and I keep the split. تَوْأَمَانِ is one of the few words the edition prints with a precomposed hamza.

sentences.t: فَالدِّينُ كَنْزٌ وَالْمُلْكُ حَارِسٌ
sentences.tr: fa-al-dīnu kanzun wa-al-mulku ḥārisun
sentences.l: so the religion a treasure and the kingship a guard,
sentences.i: religion is the treasure and kingship its guardian,

sentences.t: وَقَدْ دَلَّتِ الشَّرَائِعُ وَالْعُقُولُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ يَجِبُ عَلَى النَّاسِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا سُلْطَانًا يَدْفَعُ الظَّالِمَ عَنِ الْمَظْلُومِ وَيُنْصِفُ الضَّعِيفَ مِنَ الْقَوِيِّ وَيَكُفُّ بَأْسَ الْعَاتِي وَالْبَاغِي
sentences.tr: wa-qad dallati al-sharāʾiʿu wa-al-ʿuqūlu ʿalā annahu yajibu ʿalā al-nāsi an yattakhidhū sulṭānan yadfaʿu al-ẓālima ʿani al-maẓlūmi wa-yunṣifu al-ḍaʿīfa mina al-qawiyyi wa-yakuffu baʾsa al-ʿātī wa-al-bāghī
sentences.l: and indeed the laws and the minds have pointed to that-it is-obligatory upon the people that they take a sultan who repels the wrongdoer from the wronged, and deals-justly with the weak from the strong, and checks the might of the tyrant and the oppressor.
sentences.i: Both the revealed laws and human reason show that people must set up a ruler who keeps the wrongdoer from the wronged, gives the weak justice against the strong, and holds back the violence of the tyrant and the oppressor.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّهُ عَلَى قَدْرِ حُسْنِ أَخْلَاقِ السُّلْطَانِ يَكُونُ الزَّمَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku annahu ʿalā qadri ḥusni akhlāqi al-sulṭāni yakūnu al-zamānu
sentences.l: and know, O king, that-it, upon the measure of the goodness of the character of the sultan, is the time.
sentences.i: And know, O King, that the age is as good as the character of its sultan.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ شَيْئَانِ فِي النَّاسِ إِنْ صَلَحَا صَلَحَ النَّاسُ وَإِنْ فَسَدَا فَسَدَ النَّاسُ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu qad qāla rasūlu Allāhi ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama shayʾāni fī al-nāsi in ṣaliḥā ṣaliḥa al-nāsu wa-in fasadā fasada al-nāsu
sentences.l: for-indeed-it the messenger of God, God blessed upon him and greeted, has said: two things among the people; if they are sound, the people are sound, and if they are corrupt, the people are corrupt:
sentences.i: For the Messenger of God, God bless him and give him peace, said: there are two kinds among people; if they are righteous the people are righteous, and if they are corrupt the people are corrupt:
sentences.n: The saying that follows is attributed to the Prophet; the two 'things' are named in the next unit.

sentences.t: الْعُلَمَاءُ وَالْأُمَرَاءُ
sentences.tr: al-ʿulamāʾu wa-al-umarāʾu
sentences.l: the knowers and the commanders.
sentences.i: the scholars and the rulers.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَالَ بَعْضُ الْحُكَمَاءِ الْمُلُوكُ ثَلَٰثَةٌ مَلِكُ دِينٍ وَمَلِكُ مُحَافَظَةٍ عَلَى الْحُرُمَاتِ وَمَلِكُ هَوًي
sentences.tr: wa-qad qāla baʿḍu al-ḥukamāʾi al-mulūku thalāthatun maliku dīnin wa-maliku muḥāfaẓatin ʿalā al-ḥurumāti wa-maliku hawan
sentences.l: and indeed said some of the wise-ones: the kings are three: a king of religion, and a king of guarding over the sacred-things, and a king of desire.
sentences.i: And some of the wise have said: kings are of three kinds: a king of religion, a king who guards what is sacred, and a king of appetite.
sentences.n: ثلثة is printed in the defective spelling for ثلاثة, so I point it with the dagger alif. هوي is printed with yā' for alif maqṣūra (هَوًى 'desire, whim').

sentences.t: فَأَمَّا مَلِكُ الدِّينِ فَإِنَّهُ يُلْزِمُ رَعِينَهُ بِاتِّبَاعِ دِينِهِمْ وَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَكُونَ أَدْيَنَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ammā maliku al-dīni fa-innahu yulzimu raʿīnahu bi-ittibāʿi dīnihim wa-yanbaghī an yakūna adyanahum
sentences.l: so as-for the king of religion, indeed-he binds his flock to following of their religion, and it is fitting that he be the most-religious of them,
sentences.i: As for the king of religion, he binds his subjects to follow their faith, and he should be the most devout of them,
sentences.n: رعينه is probably a misprint for رَعِيَّتَهُ 'his subjects, his flock' (the printed letters have ن where ت is expected); I point the letters as printed.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُ هُوَ الَّذِي يُقْتَدَى بِهِ فِي أُمُورِ الدِّينِ وَيُلْزِمُ النَّاسَ طَاعَتَهُ فِيمَا أَمَرَ بِهِ مُوَافِقًا لِلْأَحْكَامِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: li-annahu huwa alladhī yuqtadā bihi fī umūri al-dīni wa-yulzimu al-nāsa ṭāʿatahu fīmā amara bihi muwāfiqan li-al-aḥkāmi al-sharʿiyyati
sentences.l: because-he, he is the one-who is-followed by-him in the affairs of the religion, and he binds the people to obedience of him in what he commanded by-it, agreeing with the rulings, the legal-ones.
sentences.i: because he is the one who is followed in matters of religion, and he binds people to obey him in whatever he commands, so long as it agrees with the rulings of the law.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنَّهُ يُنَزِّلُ السَّاخِطَ مَنْزِلَةَ الرَّاضِي بِسَبَبِ التَّسْلِيمِ إِلَى الْأَ قْدَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākinnahu yunazzilu al-sākhiṭa manzilata al-rāḍī bi-sababi al-taslīmi ilā al-aqdāri
sentences.l: but he sets down the angry-one in the station of the content-one, by reason of the submission to the decrees.
sentences.i: But he treats the resentful as though they were content, on the ground of submission to the divine decrees.
sentences.n: The print has a space inside الا قدار (al-aqdār); I keep the split.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَلِكُ مُحَافَظَةٍ عَلَى الْحُرُمَاتِ فَإِنَّهُ يَقُومُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā maliku muḥāfaẓatin ʿalā al-ḥurumāti fa-innahu yaqūmu
sentences.l: and as-for the king of guarding over the sacred-things, indeed-he stands
sentences.i: And as for the king who guards what is sacred, he takes charge

sentences.t: بِأُمُورِ الدِّينِ وَالدُّنْيَا وَيُلْزِمُ النَّاسَ بِانْبَاعِ الشَّرْعِ وَالْمُحَافَظَةِ عَلَى الْمُرُوَّةِ
sentences.tr: bi-umūri al-dīni wa-al-dunyā wa-yulzimu al-nāsa bi-inbāʿi al-sharʿi wa-al-muḥāfaẓati ʿalā al-muruwwati
sentences.l: by the affairs of the religion and the world, and binds the people to following the law and the guarding of manliness.
sentences.i: of the affairs of religion and of this world; he binds people to follow the law and to preserve their honour.
sentences.n: بانباع is a misprint for باتباع 'by following' (ن for ت); I point the letters as printed. المروة is printed without the hamza of المروءة.

sentences.t: وَيَكُونُ جَامِعًا بَيْنَ الْقَلَمِ وَالسَّيْفِ فَمَنْ زَاغَ عَمَّا سَطَرَ الْقَلَمُ زَلَّتْ بِهِ الْقَدَمُ فَيُقَوِّمُ اعْوِجَابَهُ بِحَدِّ الْحُسَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-yakūnu jāmiʿan bayna al-qalami wa-al-sayfi fa-man zāgha ʿammā saṭara al-qalamu zallat bihi al-qadamu fa-yuqawwimu iʿwijābahu bi-ḥaddi al-ḥusāmi
sentences.l: and he is combining between the pen and the sword; so whoever swerves from what the pen has written, the foot slips with him, and he straightens his crookedness by the edge of the sharp-sword,
sentences.i: He joins the pen with the sword: whoever strays from what the pen has written, his foot slips, and the king straightens his crookedness with the edge of the blade,
sentences.n: اعوجابه is a misprint for اعوجاجه 'his crookedness' (ب for ج); I point the letters as printed. The slip of the foot (زلت به القدم) is rhymed with the next clauses in a run of sajʿ.

sentences.t: وَيَنْشُرُ الْعَدْلَ فِي جَمِيعِ الْأَنَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-yanshuru al-ʿadla fī jamīʿi al-anāmi
sentences.l: and he spreads the justice among all of the mankind.
sentences.i: and spreads justice among all people.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَلِكُ الْهَوَى فَلَا دِينَ لَهُ إِلَّا اِتِّبَاعُ هَوَاهُ وَلَمْ يَخْشَ سَطْوَةَ مَوْلَاهُ الَّذِي وَلَّاهُ فَمَأٰلُ مُلْكِهِ إِلَى الدَّمَارِ وَنِهَايَةُ عَتُوِّهِ إِلَى دَارِ الْبَوَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā maliku al-hawā fa-lā dīna lahu illā ittibāʿu hawāhu wa-lam yakhsha saṭwata mawlāhu alladhī wallāhu fa-maʾālu mulkihi ilā al-damāri wa-nihāyatu ʿutuwwihi ilā dāri al-bawāri
sentences.l: And as for the king of the desire, then no religion to him except the following of his desire, and he did not fear the wrath of his master who appointed him; so the outcome of his kingdom is to the ruin, and the end of his insolence to the abode of the perdition,
sentences.i: As for a king ruled by his own desires, he has no religion but the pursuit of his whims, and he never feared the wrath of the Master who gave him his throne. So his kingdom ends in ruin, and his arrogance in the abode of perdition.
sentences.n: This sentence begins before this stretch; the slice picks it up midway. فَمَأٰلُ is printed فمأل: the alif of مَآل "outcome" is not written, so it is read with a dagger alif, as the two balanced phrases (the outcome of his kingdom ... the end of his insolence) require. مَوْلَاهُ "his master" is God, who set the king in power. The two clauses end in the same rhyme, الدَّمَار / الْبَوَار.

sentences.t: وَقٰلَتِ الْحُكَمَاءُ الْمَلِكُ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى كَثِيرٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَهُمْ مُحْتَاجُونَ إِلَى وَاحِدٍ وَلِأَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ وَجَبَ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَارِفًا بِأَخْلَاقِهِمْ لِيَرُدَّ اِخْتِلَافَهُمْ إِلَى وِفَاتِهِمْ وَيَعُمَّهُمْ بِعَدْ لِهِ وَيَغْمُرَهُمْ بِفَضْلِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālati al-ḥukamāʾu al-maliku yaḥtāju ilā kathīrin mina al-nāsi wa-hum muḥtājūna ilā wāḥidin wa-li-ajli dhālika wajaba an yakūna ʿārifan bi-akhlāqihim li-yaruddu ikhtilāfahum ilā wifātihim wa-yaʿummahum bi-ʿad li-hi wa-yaghmurahum bi-faḍlihi
sentences.l: And the sages said: The king needs many of the people, and they are needing one; and for the sake of that it was necessary that he be knowing with their characters, in order to bring back their discord to their concord, and embrace them with his justice, and flood them with his bounty.
sentences.i: The sages have said that the king needs a great many people, while they all need only one man. For that reason he must understand their natures, so as to turn their quarrels back into agreement, to embrace them all with his justice and flood them with his generosity.
sentences.n: وِفَاتِهِمْ is printed وفاتهم; the sense calls for وفاقهم "their concord" (a misprint of ق as ت), and the printed letters are kept. بعد له is printed as two words, for بعدله "with his justice"; the split is kept, and the glossary gives the two pieces separately. عَارِفًا بِـ is "acquainted with"; the verb takes bi-. Here the sages' saying runs through four balanced clauses.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ أَزْدَ شِيرَ يُقَالُ لَهُ جَمْرُ شَدِيدٍ وَهُوَ الثَّالِثُ مِنْ مُلُوكِ الْفُرْسِ قٰلَ مَلَكَ الْأَقَالِيمَ جَمِيعَهَا وَقَسَّمَهَا عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْسَامٍ وَجَعَلَ لَهُ مِنْ أَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ أَرْبَعَ خَوَاتِمَ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna azda shīra yuqālu lahu jamru shadīdin wa-huwa al-thālithu min mulūki al-furs qāla malaka al-aqālīma jamīʿahā wa-qassamahā ʿalā arbaʿati aqsāmin wa-jaʿala lahu min ajli dhālika arbaʿa khawātima
sentences.l: And know, O king, that Azdashīr, it is said to him Jamr Shadīd, and he is the third of the kings of the Persians, said: He ruled the regions, all of them, and divided them upon four parts, and made, for the sake of that, four seals,
sentences.i: And know, O king, that Ardashīr, who is called Jamr Shadīd, was the third of the kings of the Persians. It is told that he ruled all the lands, divided them into four parts, and for that purpose made four seals,
sentences.n: ازد شير is printed as two words; it is the Persian king Ardashīr, and the split is kept. "Jamr Shadīd" ("fierce ember") is how the print has the second name, probably a corrupt form of Jamshīd; the text cannot settle it here. قل is printed for قال; it is read قٰلَ "he said" with the dagger alif, though the sense of the clause is "it is told that he ruled". مَلَكَ الْأَقَالِيمَ جَمِيعَهَا is "ruled the regions, all of them", the noun jamīʿ placed after what it describes. مِنْ أَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ is "for that reason".

sentences.t: لِكُلِّ قِسْمٍ حَاتِمٌ الْأَوَّلُ خَاتِمُ الْبَصَرِ وَالشُّرْطَةِ وَالْمُحَامَةِ وَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ النِّيَابَاتِ
sentences.tr: li-kulli qismin ḥātimun al-awwalu khātimu al-baṣari wa-al-shurṭati wa-al-muḥāmati wa-kataba ʿalayhi al-niyābāti
sentences.l: For each part a seal: the first, the seal of the sight and the police and the defence, and he wrote on it the deputyships;
sentences.i: Each part had its seal. The first was the seal of oversight, of the guard and of defence, and on it he wrote the offices of deputy.
sentences.n: حَاتِمٌ is printed حاتم, an obvious misprint of خاتم "seal"; the printed letter is kept. Two lines on, the same word is spelt خاتم correctly. المحامة is printed with one alif; it probably stands for المحاماة "the defence". The sentence is an elliptical list: the text gives each seal its sphere and what was written on it.

sentences.t: وَالثَّانِي خَاتِمُ الْخَرَاجِ وَجِبَايَةِ الْأَمْوَالِ وَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْعِمَارَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-thānī khātimu al-kharāji wa-jibāyati al-amwāli wa-kataba ʿalayhi al-ʿimārata
sentences.l: and the second, the seal of the land-tax and the collection of the monies, and he wrote on it the cultivation;
sentences.i: The second was the seal of the land-tax and the gathering of revenue, and on it he wrote prosperity.
sentences.n: الْعِمَارَة is the upbuilding of the land, that is, tilled fields and settled towns: the thing the tax is meant to serve.

sentences.t: وَالثَّالِثُ خَانِمُ الْقُوتِ وَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ الرَّخَاءَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-thālithu khānimu al-qūti wa-kataba ʿalayhi al-rakhāʾa
sentences.l: and the third, the seal of the sustenance, and he wrote on it the plenty;
sentences.i: The third was the seal of provisions, and on it he wrote plenty.
sentences.n: خَانِمُ is printed خانم, a misprint of خاتم "seal" (ت for ن); the printed letters are kept.

sentences.t: وَالرَّابِعُ خَاتِمُ الْمَظَالِمِ وَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْعَدْلَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-rābiʿu khātimu al-maẓālimi wa-kataba ʿalayhi al-ʿadla
sentences.l: and the fourth, the seal of the grievances, and he wrote on it the justice;
sentences.i: The fourth was the seal of grievances, and on it he wrote justice.
sentences.n: الْمَظَالِم are complaints of wrong done, brought to the ruler for redress; the seal's motto is therefore العدل "justice".

sentences.t: فَبَقِيَتْ وَاسْتَمَرَّتْ هٰذِهِ الرُّسُومُ فِي الْفُرْسِ إِلَى أَنْ ظَهَرَ الْإِسْلَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-baqiyat wa-istamarrat hādhihi al-rusūmu fī al-furs ilā an ẓahara al-islāmu
sentences.l: so these customs remained and continued among the Persians until Islam appeared,
sentences.i: These customs lasted and endured among the Persians until Islam came.
sentences.n: The verbs فَبَقِيَتْ وَاسْتَمَرَّتْ are feminine because الرُّسُوم, a plural of things, takes feminine singular agreement. The two verbs say nearly the same thing, a doubling typical of this style.

sentences.t: وَكَتَبَ كِسْرَى لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ فِي جَيْشِهِ لَاتُوَسِّعَنَّ عَلَى جَيْشِكَ فَيَسْتَغْنُوا عَنْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kataba kisrā li-ibnihi wa-huwa fī jayshihi lā-tuwassiʿanna ʿalā jayshika fa-yastaghnū ʿanka
sentences.l: and Kisrā wrote to his son, while he was in his army: Do not widen upon your army, lest they do-without from you,
sentences.i: And Khosrow wrote to his son, who was with his army: "Do not be too lavish with your troops, or they will come to feel they have no need of you."
sentences.n: The letter is quoted straight, with no "saying". لَاتُوَسِّعَنَّ is written as one word; it carries the print's own shadda on the final nūn (the emphatic ending). تَوَسَّعَ عَلَى is "be generous to, give liberal allowance to". فَيَسْتَغْنُوا عَنْكَ is "that they come to need you not". The sentence is cut short by the end of the night.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night: morning overtakes Shahrazād and she stops the "permitted speech", the story she was allowed to tell.
